items.q: Stock B was bought at 35.84 with a stop at 34.62. On May 7 it opened at 34.47, below the stop. What is the result in R, if the stop filled at the open?
items.explain: The loss per share is 35.84 - 34.47 = 1.37 and one R is 1.22, so the result is -1.12R. A gap through the stop costs more than 1R.

items.explain: The stock is in an uptrend above a rising 50-day average, it pulled back for five days to the 20-day average, and the last bar closed above the previous high. That is the trend pullback trigger.

items.q: Stock B broke out on April 10 and was bought at 31.94. On April 15 it closes at 31.01, under the pivot of 31.13, and its low of 30.94 is above the stop of 30.68. What does the setup say to do?
choices: Hold, because the stop was not hit
Buy more at the lower price
items.explain: Rule 7 says that any close under the pivot before the target means a sale at the next open. Here that is 30.91 on April 16, a loss of 0.82R.

range: 2025-10-01 to 2026-02-06
items.q: On January 23, 2026, Index X closes at 3,347.24 and its 200-day average is about 4,165. What does the 200-day filter say about new long trades?
choices: Favourable: take pullback and breakout setups
Unfavourable: no new pullback or breakout longs
items.explain: The close is under the average, so trend is unfavourable. The index first closed under its average on December 16, 2025, and did not close above it again until April 27, 2026.

items.q: Index X first closes under its 200-day average on December 16, 2025 and next closes above it on April 27, 2026. How many sessions was it under, counting December 16?
items.explain: From December 16, 2025 to April 24, 2026 there are 94 sessions. A trader who took new longs only above the average took none in that time.

items.explain: The exit is the close of the first session above the 5-day average, here March 5 at 58.48. With an entry of 56.41 and a risk of 1.89 per share, that is +1.10R.
